title: CARP: Range Query-Optimized Indexing for Streaming Data
problem: High-performance scientific applications generate massive data volumes that stress storage resources. Efficient range-based analyses require expensive post-processing sorts, while in-situ indexing techniques are write-efficient but orders of magnitude slower than sorted indices for range queries.
motivation: Range queries are essential for analyzing continuous physical attributes and tracking phenomena like energy bands and wave fronts in scientific data.
method: CARP dynamically partitions data in-situ as it streams to storage during application I/O. It discovers and adapts data partitions to track skewed and dynamic characteristics of real application distributions. The system reorders data during streaming ingestion without post-processing overhead, approximating the query performance of fully sorted indices.
key_novelty: Dynamic discovery and adaptation of data partitions during streaming to handle skewed and dynamic distributions, enabling sorted-index-level query performance without ingestion overhead.
contributions: Scalable data partitioner for range queries on streaming scientific data
Dynamic partition adaptation mechanism that tracks skewed and dynamic distributions
In-situ reordering during I/O without ingestion overhead
5x speedup over prior in-situ indexing approaches
limitations: Limitations of the approach not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Adaptive data partitioning for streaming range queries
